concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with place values powers of two, possibly padded with leading zeros to a fixed length.

concepts.name: Logarithms and floor/ceiling
concepts.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and rounding functions used to count bits and levels of recursion.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic of integers where numbers are identified when they differ by a multiple of a modulus.

concepts.name: Primes and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Prime numbers and pairs of integers with no common factor other than 1.

concepts.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Finite-dimensional linear algebra including invertible maps, linear combinations, subspaces and rank.

concepts.name: Tensor (Kronecker) product and multidimensional arrays

concepts.name: Roots of unity
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers w with w^n = 1, such as e^{2 pi i/n}.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and basic divide-and-conquer
concepts.gloss: The quadratic digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm and the idea of splitting a problem into smaller recursive calls.

concepts.name: Recurrence relations and geometric sums
concepts.gloss: Solving running-time recurrences and summing geometric series to bound recursive algorithms.

concepts.name: Floating and fixed-point numbers and rounding
concepts.gloss: Finite-precision representation of real numbers and bounding the error of approximations, including the maximum norm of a vector.

concepts.name: Sorting and permutations
concepts.gloss: Rearranging items by a permutation, and the bitwise exclusive-or operation on bit strings.

concepts.name: Asymptotic notation variants
concepts.gloss: Theta and Omega notation for tight and lower bounds, and worst-case time complexity.

concepts.name: Finite sets, products and maps
concepts.gloss: Basic set theory including products of sets, bijections, and integers modulo m as an index set.

background.summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis including recurrences and logarithms, basic discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, binary representation, divisibility and primes), linear algebra (vectors, matrices, tensor-like indexing of arrays), and elementary algorithms such as schoolbook multiplication. They know Turing machines and tapes, polynomials and complex numbers, but have not studied fast integer multiplication, the FFT in depth, number-theoretic transforms, finite fields, or abstract algebra beyond basics. Specialist material introduced by the paper is not assumed.
